GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.pstarL2_mul_piL2.doc: `P⋆ Π = Π`: the function action fixes the constants.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.pstarL2_apply.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), (L.pstarL2 hrow) F = L.pstarLp F

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.pstarL2.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} →
    (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) →
      GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.pstarL2.doc:
**`P⋆` as a bounded linear operator on `L²(μ)`**, of norm at most `1`.

This is the `p = 2` case of `lem:doubling_operator`(1)'s first clause, and the operator that
`lem:doubling_operator`(3) — proved abstractly in `Operator.lean` — is instantiated at
(`UnboundedL2.lean`). The adjoint clause `P⋆ = P*` is `Stat.adjoint_pstarL2` (`AdjointL2.lean`).

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.pos.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (self : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄,
  GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → 0 < self.lam x

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.piL2_mul_pstarL2.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap), L.piL2 * L.pstarL2 hrow = L.piL2
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.piL2_mul_pstarL2.doc: `Π P⋆ = Π`: the function action preserves the `λ`-mean.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.piL2_mul_piL2.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap), L.piL2 * L.piL2 = L.piL2

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.piL2_mul_densL2.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap), L.piL2 * L.densL2 hrow = L.piL2
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.piL2_mul_densL2.doc: `Π P = Π`, read off the adjoint of `P Π = Π`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.piL2_fixed_of_ps.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) {F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)}, (L.pstarL2 hrow) F = F → L.piL2 F = F
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.piL2_fixed_of_ps.doc:
**`hker`**: `P⋆f = f` forces `Πf = f`. This is the hypothesis
`OperatorFinite.exists_resolvent` consumes in place of irreducibility.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.piL2_apply.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), L.piL2 F = inner ℝ L.oneLp F • L.oneLp

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.piL2.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} →
    (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.percut_K.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)) {B : ℝ} {m : ℕ},
  S.d < m →
    GFNBounds.Doubling.HasDouble (some K) m →
      (∀ (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
          (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
            ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * f x = 0 →
              L.mass 2 f ≤ B * L.mass 2 fun x => f x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S (some K) f x) →
        L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m) ≤ 2 * L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad m) * B
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.percut_K.doc:
**`eq:doubling_percut_K`, squared and cleared.** Every constant bounding the `L²(λ^K)`
Rayleigh quotient is at least `L_K(m)(1−L_K(m)) / (2λ^K_m)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.orthogonal_defec.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none), L.defectRangeᗮ = ℝ ∙ L.oneLp
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.orthogonal_defec.doc: **The orthogonal complement of the range of `Id − P⋆` is the line of constants.**

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.oneLp_mem_orthog.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none), L.oneLp ∈ L.defectRangeᗮ

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.oneLp.type: {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} → {cap : Option ℕ} → (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.oneLp.doc: The constant function `1` as an element of `L²(μ)`; `μ` is a probability.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.not_tendsto_part.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S →
    ¬∃ U, Filter.Tendsto (GFNBounds.Doubling.partialSum (L.pstarL2 ⋯) L.piL2) Filter.atTop (nhds U)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.not_tendsto_part.doc:
**`theo:doubling_unbounded`(2) at `p = 2`: the series does not converge in operator norm.**
The partial sums `Σ_{n<N}(P⋆ⁿ − Π)` have no limit in `L²(λ) →L L²(λ)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.not_summable_bet.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S → ¬Summable (L.betaHat ⋯)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.not_summable_bet.doc:
**`theo:doubling_unbounded`(2) at `p = 2`: `Σ β̂_n = +∞`.** The mixing coefficients
`β̂_n = ‖Pⁿ − Π‖_{L²(λ)}` are not summable.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.norm_sq_eq_mass_.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  {F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)} {g : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  ↑↑F =ᵐ[L.mu] g → MeasureTheory.MemLp g 2 L.mu → ‖F‖ ^ 2 = L.mass 2 g
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.norm_sq_eq_mass_.doc: The `L²` norm squared of a class is the `mass` of any of its representatives, at every `cap`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.norm_sq_eq_mass.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) {F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)}
  {g : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ}, ↑↑F =ᵐ[L.mu] g → MeasureTheory.MemLp g 2 L.mu → ‖F‖ ^ 2 = L.mass 2 g
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.norm_sq_eq_mass.doc: The `L²` norm squared of a class is the `mass` of any of its representatives.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.norm_pstarLp_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), ‖L.pstarLp F‖ ≤ ‖F‖

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.norm_pstarL2_pow.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (n : ℕ), ‖L.pstarL2 hrow ^ n - L.piL2‖ = L.betaHat hrow n
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.norm_pstarL2_pow.doc:
**`‖P⋆ⁿ − Π‖_{L²(λ)} = β̂ₙ` for every `n ≥ 0`** — the trailing clause of
`lem:doubling_operator`(1). `Π` is self-adjoint because `λ` is a probability, so `P⋆ⁿ − Π` is the
adjoint of `Pⁿ − Π`, and taking adjoints is an isometry.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.norm_pstarL2_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap), ‖L.pstarL2 hrow‖ ≤ 1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.norm_oneLp.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap), ‖L.oneLp‖ = 1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.norm_densLp_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), ‖L.densLp hrow F‖ ≤ ‖F‖

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.norm_densL2_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap), ‖L.densL2 hrow‖ ≤ 1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.nonneg.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (self : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St),
  0 ≤ self.lam x

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.no_diffusionOp.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S → ¬∃ Sop, Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 ⋯) = 1 - L.piL2
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.no_diffusionOp.doc:
**`theo:doubling_unbounded`(2) at `p = 2`, the convention `B̂ = +∞`.** No bounded operator `S`
on `L²(λ)` satisfies `S(Id − P⋆) = Id − Π`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.no_bounded_inver.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) {γ : ℝ},
  (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → (↑j + 1) * S.eps j ≤ γ) →
    ¬∃ B,
        ∀ (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ) (M D : ℝ),
          (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
            ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * f x = 0 →
              (∃ x, M ≤ |f x|) →
                (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S none f x| ≤ D) → M ≤ B * D
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.no_bounded_inver.doc:
**`lem:doubling_ramp`, the conclusion.** No constant `B` bounds an attained lower bound of
`‖f‖_∞` by a uniform upper bound of `‖(Id−P⋆)f‖_∞` over the **bounded** mean-zero `f`: the
clipped ramps drive the `L^∞` Rayleigh quotient to zero. A bounded `S` on `L^∞(λ)` with
`S(Id−P⋆) = Id−Π` would supply `B = ‖S‖` for exactly these `f`, so this is the paper's "no bounded
`S`". The witnesses are the centred clipped ramps, bounded by `centredRamp_bounded`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.no_bounded_inver.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S →
    ∀ {p : ℝ},
      1 ≤ p →
        ¬∃ B,
            ∀ (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
              (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
                ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * f x = 0 →
                  L.mass p f ≤ B * L.mass p fun x => f x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S none f x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.no_bounded_inver.doc:
**Step 3 of `theo:doubling_unbounded`(2).** No constant bounds the mass of a bounded mean-zero
function by the mass of its flow-matching defect: in `L^p(λ)` terms, no bounded `S` satisfies
`S(Id − P⋆) = Id − Π`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.noConfusionType.type:
Sort u →
  {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
    {cap : Option ℕ} →
      GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap →
        {S' : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} → {cap' : Option ℕ} → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S' cap' → Sort u

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.noConfusion.type:
{P : Sort u} →
  {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
    {cap : Option ℕ} →
      {t : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap} →
        {S' : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
          {cap' : Option ℕ} →
            {t' : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S' cap'} →
              S = S' → cap = cap' → t ≍ t' → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.noConfusionType P t t'

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mu_singleton_ne_.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St},
  L.mu {x} ≠ 0 ↔ GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mu_singleton_ne_.doc: `μ` charges exactly the states of the chain.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mu_singleton.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St),
  L.mu {x} = ENNReal.ofReal (L.lam x)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mu.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap → MeasureTheory.Measure GFNBounds.Doubling.St
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mu.doc: **The measure `λ` carries**, as a measure on `St`: the counting measure weighted by `λ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mk.sizeOf_spec.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (lam : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ)
  (nonneg : ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), 0 ≤ lam x)
  (pos : ∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → 0 < lam x)
  (vanish : ∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, ¬GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → lam x = 0) (summable : Summable lam)
  (total : ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x = 1)
  (inv :
    ∀ (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
      (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
        ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x =
          ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x * f x),
  sizeOf
      { lam := lam, nonneg := nonneg, pos := pos, vanish := vanish, summable := summable, total := total, inv := inv } =
    1 + sizeOf summable + sizeOf total

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mk.noConfusion.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} →
    {P : Sort u} →
      {lam : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ} →
        {nonneg : ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), 0 ≤ lam x} →
          {pos : ∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → 0 < lam x} →
            {vanish : ∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, ¬GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → lam x = 0} →
              {summable : Summable lam} →
                {total : ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x = 1} →
                  {inv :
                      ∀ (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
                        (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
                          ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x =
                            ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x * f x} →
                    {lam' : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ} →
                      {nonneg' : ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), 0 ≤ lam' x} →
                        {pos' : ∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → 0 < lam' x} →
                          {vanish' : ∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, ¬GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → lam' x = 0} →
                            {summable' : Summable lam'} →
                              {total' : ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam' x = 1} →
                                {inv' :
                                    ∀ (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
                                      (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
                                        ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam' x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x =
                                          ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam' x * f x} →
                                  { lam := lam, nonneg := nonneg, pos := pos, vanish := vanish, summable := summable,
                                        total := total, inv := inv } =
                                      { lam := lam', nonneg := nonneg', pos := pos', vanish := vanish',
                                        summable := summable', total := total', inv := inv' } →
                                    (lam = lam' → P) → P

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mk.injEq.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (lam : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ)
  (nonneg : ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), 0 ≤ lam x)
  (pos : ∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → 0 < lam x)
  (vanish : ∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, ¬GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → lam x = 0) (summable : Summable lam)
  (total : ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x = 1)
  (inv :
    ∀ (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
      (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
        ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x =
          ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x * f x)
  (lam_1 : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ) (nonneg_1 : ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), 0 ≤ lam_1 x)
  (pos_1 : ∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → 0 < lam_1 x)
  (vanish_1 : ∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, ¬GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → lam_1 x = 0)
  (summable_1 : Summable lam_1) (total_1 : ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam_1 x = 1)
  (inv_1 :
    ∀ (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
      (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
        ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam_1 x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x =
          ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam_1 x * f x),
  ({ lam := lam, nonneg := nonneg, pos := pos, vanish := vanish, summable := summable, total := total, inv := inv } =
      { lam := lam_1, nonneg := nonneg_1, pos := pos_1, vanish := vanish_1, summable := summable_1, total := total_1,
        inv := inv_1 }) =
    (lam = lam_1)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mk.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} →
    (lam : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ) →
      (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), 0 ≤ lam x) →
        (∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → 0 < lam x) →
          (∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, ¬GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → lam x = 0) →
            Summable lam →
              ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x = 1 →
                (∀ (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
                    (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
                      ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x =
                        ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x * f x) →
                  GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mem_kerPi_iff.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) {F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)},
  F ∈ L.kerPi ↔ ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * ↑↑F x = 0
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mem_kerPi_iff.doc: `ker Π` is what its name says: `F` has zero mean.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.memLp_two_pstar.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 L.mu → MeasureTheory.MemLp (GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f) 2 L.mu

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.memLp_two_of_bou.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) → MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.memLp_two_of_bou.doc: A bounded function is in `L²(λ)`: `λ` is a probability.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.memLp_two_iff.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 L.mu ↔ Summable fun x => |f x| ^ 2 * L.lam x

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.memLp_pstar.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {p : ENNReal},
  1 ≤ p →
    p ≠ ⊤ →
      ∀ {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
        MeasureTheory.MemLp f p L.mu → MeasureTheory.MemLp (GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f) p L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.memLp_pstar.doc: `P⋆` maps `L^p(μ)` into itself, at every finite `p ≥ 1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.memLp_iff.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ}
  {p : ENNReal}, p ≠ 0 → p ≠ ⊤ → (MeasureTheory.MemLp f p L.mu ↔ Summable fun x => |f x| ^ p.toReal * L.lam x)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.memLp_iff.doc: **`f ∈ L^p(μ)` iff its `p`-th power mass converges.**

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.memLp_dens.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ {p : ENNReal},
      1 ≤ p →
        p ≠ ⊤ → ∀ {u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ}, MeasureTheory.MemLp u p L.mu → MeasureTheory.MemLp (L.dens u) p L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.memLp_dens.doc: `P` maps `L^p(μ)` into itself, at every finite `p ≥ 1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.memLp_centredTai.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (m : ℕ),
  MeasureTheory.MemLp (L.centredTail m) 2 L.mu

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_two_pstar_l.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  (Summable fun x => |f x| ^ 2 * L.lam x) → L.mass 2 (GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f) ≤ L.mass 2 f
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_two_pstar_l.doc: **`P⋆` contracts the `L²(λ)` mass.** Jensen (`sq_pstar_le`) pointwise, then invariance.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_two_centred.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (m : ℕ),
  L.mass 2 (L.centredTail m) = L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_two_centred.doc:
**`‖f_m‖²_{L²(λ)} = L(1−L)`**, exactly — the denominator of `eq:doubling_step3`.

The two terms of `mass_centredTail` collapse: `L(1−L)² + (1−L)L² = L(1−L)[(1−L) + L]`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_ratio_bound.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {m : ℕ},
  S.d < m →
    GFNBounds.Doubling.HasDouble cap m →
      ∀ {p : ℝ},
        1 ≤ p →
          0 < L.tailMass m →
            1 / 2 ≤ 1 - L.tailMass m →
              ∀ {t : ℝ},
                0 < t →
                  2 * L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad m) ≤ t * (L.tailMass m * (1 / 2) ^ p) →
                    (L.mass p fun x => L.centredTail m x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap (L.centredTail m) x) ≤
                      t * L.mass p (L.centredTail m)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_ratio_bound.doc:
The mass ratio at one cut: `mass p ((Id−P⋆)f_m) ≤ 2λ_m` against `mass p f_m ≥ L(m)·2^{-p}`.
This is `eq:doubling_stepp` read as a ratio.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_pstar_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {p : ℝ},
  1 ≤ p →
    ∀ {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
      (Summable fun x => |f x| ^ p * L.lam x) → L.mass p (GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f) ≤ L.mass p f
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_pstar_le.doc:
**`‖P⋆v‖_{L^p(λ)} ≤ ‖v‖_{L^p(λ)}` on the plain-real layer**, at every `p ≥ 1`: Jensen
pointwise, then invariance against `|v|^p`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_nonneg.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ)
  {r : ℝ}, 0 ≤ L.mass r f

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_le_of_rayle.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) {B : ℝ},
  (∀ (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), ‖F - L.piL2 F‖ ≤ B * ‖F - (L.pstarL2 hrow) F‖) →
    ∀ {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
      (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
        ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * f x = 0 →
          L.mass 2 f ≤ B ^ 2 * L.mass 2 fun x => f x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_le_of_rayle.doc:
**The bridge.** If `‖F − ΠF‖ ≤ B‖F − P⋆F‖` on `L²(λ)`, then every bounded mean-zero `f` has
`mass 2 f ≤ B² · mass 2 ((Id − P⋆)f)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_le_of_leftI.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) {Sop : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)},
  Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) = 1 - L.piL2 →
    ∀ {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
      (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
        ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * f x = 0 →
          L.mass 2 f ≤ ‖Sop‖ ^ 2 * L.mass 2 fun x => f x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_le_of_leftI.doc: The bridge, fed by a left inverse: `mass 2 f ≤ ‖S‖² · mass 2 ((Id − P⋆)f)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_dens_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ {p : ℝ},
      1 ≤ p →
        ∀ {u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ}, (Summable fun x => |u x| ^ p * L.lam x) → L.mass p (L.dens u) ≤ L.mass p u
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_dens_le.doc:
**`P` is a contraction of `L^p(λ)`**, `p ∈ [1,∞)` — the mirror of `Stat.mass_pstar_le`, and
what makes `P` an operator of `L²(λ)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_defect_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {m : ℕ},
  S.d < m →
    GFNBounds.Doubling.HasDouble cap m →
      ∀ {p : ℝ},
        1 ≤ p →
          (L.mass p fun x => L.centredTail m x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap (L.centredTail m) x) ≤
            2 * L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad m)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_defect_le.doc:
**The numerator of `eq:doubling_step3`.** `‖(Id − P⋆)f_m‖^p_{L^p(λ)} ≤ 2 λ_m`, for every
`p ∈ [1,∞)` and on either chain.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_congr_onCha.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (p : ℝ)
  {f g : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → f x = g x) → L.mass p f = L.mass p g
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_congr_onCha.doc:
Masses only see the chain: `λ` vanishes off it, so two functions agreeing on the chain have
the same `L^p(λ)` mass. This is what lets the off-chain failure of `percut_id` be harmless.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_centredTail.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ),
  L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m) ^ p ≤ L.mass p (L.centredTail m)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_centredTail.doc: The denominator of `eq:doubling_step3`, bounded below: `‖f_m‖^p ≥ L(1−L)^p`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_centredTail.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {m : ℕ},
  S.d < m →
    GFNBounds.Doubling.HasDouble cap m →
      ∀ (p : ℝ),
        (L.mass p fun x => L.centredTail m x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap (L.centredTail m) x) =
          L.mass p (GFNBounds.Doubling.cutFn S m)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_centredTail.doc: The `L^p(λ)` mass of `(Id − P⋆)f_m` is that of the per-cut defect.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_centredTail.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ),
  L.mass p (L.centredTail m) = L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m) ^ p + (1 - L.tailMass m) * L.tailMass m ^ p
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass_centredTail.doc:
**`eq:doubling_stepp`, second line.** `‖f_m‖^p_{L^p(λ)} = L(1−L)^p + (1−L)L^p`.

⚠ weakened hypothesis: the paper states this for `p ∈ [1,∞)`, but the identity needs nothing about
`p` at all — `f_m` takes only the two values `1 − L` and `−L`, so the computation is exact at every
exponent. The hypothesis is dropped rather than carried unused.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap → ℝ → (GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ) → ℝ
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mass.doc: The `p`-th power of the `L^p(λ)` norm, in plain `ℝ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mact_lam.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.mact S cap L.lam y = L.lam y
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.mact_lam.doc:
**`λT = λ`, pointwise.** The paper's invariance hypothesis is carried in `Stat` in the
integral form against bounded test functions; testing it against the indicator of a single state
and reading the duality identity on the other side gives the balance equation at that state.

This is the identity `PointwiseInv.inv_of_pointwise` *assumes*; here it is derived.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lintegral_rpow_e.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ)
  {r : ℝ},
  0 ≤ r →
    (Summable fun x => |f x| ^ r * L.lam x) →
      ∫⁻ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), ‖f x‖ₑ ^ r ∂L.mu = ENNReal.ofReal (L.mass r f)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lintegral_rpow_e.doc: **`Stat.mass` is the `L^p` integrand's total mass**, whenever that mass is finite.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lintegral_rpow_e.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ)
  {r : ℝ},
  0 ≤ r →
    ∫⁻ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), ‖f x‖ₑ ^ r ∂L.mu =
      ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), ENNReal.ofReal (|f x| ^ r * L.lam x)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lintegral_rpow_e.doc: The `p`-th power integrand of `eLpNorm`, on the plain-real layer.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lintegral_eq_tsu.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (g : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ENNReal),
  ∫⁻ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), g x ∂L.mu = ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), g x * ENNReal.ofReal (L.lam x)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_src_le_lam_o.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0) ≤ L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 1)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_sink_eq_src.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  L.lam GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink = L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_sink.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  L.lam GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink = L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_sink.doc: The balance equation at the sink: `λ(s_f) = λ(s₀)`, the wrap being the only incoming edge.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_pow_two_ge.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (D : ℕ),
  L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 1) * ∏ i ∈ Finset.range D, S.eps (2 ^ i) ≤ L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (2 ^ D))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_pow_two_ge.doc: `λ_{2^D} ≥ λ_1 · ∏_{i<D} ε(2^i)`: iterate `eq:doubling_ratios` along the powers of two.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_one_le_coTai.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {m : ℕ},
  1 < m → L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 1) ≤ 1 - L.tailMass m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_one_le_coTai.doc: `λ_1 ≤ 1 − L(m)`: the state `1` lies outside the tail, since `m > d ≥ 1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_one_ge.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {c : ℝ},
  0 < c →
    c < 1 →
      (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / (↑j + 1)) →
        ∀ {M : ℝ}, (∀ (n : ℕ), L.hitInt n ≤ M) → (2 + S.jbar / (1 - c))⁻¹ ≤ L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 1)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_one_ge.doc: **Step 6 of `cor:doubling_truncation`.** `λ_1 ≥ (2 + j̄/(1−c))^{-1}`, a bound free of `K`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_mul_dens.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ (u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ) (y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St),
      L.lam y * L.dens u y = GFNBounds.Doubling.mact S cap (fun x => L.lam x * u x) y
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_mul_dens.doc:
**`λ·Pu = (uλ)T`.** On the chain this is the definition with the division cleared; off it both
sides vanish, `λ` by `Stat.vanish` and the transported measure by `mact_vanish_offChain`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_le_tailMass.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {m : ℕ},
  GFNBounds.Doubling.inTail cap m m → L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad m) ≤ L.tailMass m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_le_tailMass.doc: `λ_m ≤ L(m)`: the cut itself lies in the tail.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_le_prev.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {m : ℕ},
  1 ≤ m → L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad m) * (1 - S.eps m) ≤ L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (m - 1))

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_lad.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (k : ℕ),
  L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad k) =
    (L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (k + 1)) * GFNBounds.Doubling.decW S cap (k + 1) +
        if 1 ≤ k ∧ 2 ∣ k then L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (k / 2)) * GFNBounds.Doubling.dblW S cap (k / 2)
        else 0) +
      L.lam GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink * S.row k
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_lad.doc: The balance equation at a ladder state, written out.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_ge_prev.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)) {i : ℕ},
  S.d < i →
    GFNBounds.Doubling.HasDouble (some K) i →
      2 ≤ i → L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (i - 1)) * S.eps (i - 1) ≤ L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad i)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_ge_prev.doc:
**The step down, from the cut balance.** `λ_{i−1} ε(i−1) ≤ λ_i`: keeping only the term
`y = i−1` of `eq:doubling_cut` at `i`, which is legitimate because `i−1 ∈ W(i)` for `i ≥ 2`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_double_ge.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {j : ℕ},
  1 ≤ j →
    GFNBounds.Doubling.HasDouble cap j →
      L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j) * S.eps j ≤ L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (2 * j))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_double_ge.doc:
**`eq:doubling_ratios`, first half.** `λ_{2j} ≥ λ_j ε(j)`: the doubling edge out of `j`
deposits at least its own share at `2j`, whatever else arrives there.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_chain_up.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)) {j : ℕ},
  1 ≤ j →
    ∀ (n : ℕ), L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (j + n)) ≤ L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j) * (1 - S.epsMax)⁻¹ ^ n
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_chain_up.doc: Going up the ladder: `λ_{j+n} ≤ λ_j ρ^n` with `ρ = (1 − ε_max)^{-1}`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_chain_down.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)) {η : ℝ},
  0 ≤ η →
    ∀ {j : ℕ} (n : ℕ),
      (∀ (i : ℕ),
          j ≤ i → i < j + n → S.d < i + 1 ∧ GFNBounds.Doubling.HasDouble (some K) (i + 1) ∧ 1 ≤ i ∧ η ≤ S.eps i) →
        L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j) * η ^ n ≤ L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (j + n))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam_chain_down.doc:
Going up the ladder from below: `λ_j η^n ≤ λ_{j+n}` when `η` is a lower bound for `ε` on the
range crossed.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.lam.type: {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} → {cap : Option ℕ} → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap → GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.ker_eq_const.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ {u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
      (Summable fun x => |u x| ^ 2 * L.lam x) →
        ((∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → L.dens u x = u x) ↔
            ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → u x = u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0)) ∧
          ((∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St),
              GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap u x = u x) ↔
            ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → u x = u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.ker_eq_const.doc:
**`eq:doubling_fixed`, both halves.** In `L²(λ)`, the fixed points of the density action and
of the function action are exactly the functions constant on the chain — that is, `ℝ·1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.kerPi.type: {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} → (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) → Submodule ℝ ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.kerPi.doc: **`ker Π`**, the classes of `L²(λ)` of zero `λ`-mean.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.kac_identity.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {M B : ℝ},
  (∀ (n : ℕ), L.hitInt n ≤ M) →
    (∀ (n : ℕ), GFNBounds.Doubling.sbar S cap n ≤ B) →
      L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0) * (2 + ⨆ n, GFNBounds.Doubling.sbar S cap n) = 1
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.kac_identity.doc:
**Kac's formula on the doubling graph.** With `σ̄ := ⨆ₙ σ̄⁽ⁿ⁾`, `λ(s₀)(2 + σ̄) = 1`.

The hypothesis `hM` — the truncated hitting expectations are uniformly bounded in the `λ`-mean —
holds on every truncation, with `M = K/(1−c)` by `lem:doubling_supersolution`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.jensen_gap_zero_.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 L.mu →
    (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x = f x) →
      ∀ {x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St},
        GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x →
          GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap (fun y => f y ^ 2) x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x ^ 2 = 0
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.jensen_gap_zero_.doc: Equality in Jensen at every state of the chain, for a fixed point in `L²(λ)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.jensen_gap_zero.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
    GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f = f →
      ∀ {x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St},
        GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x →
          GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap (fun y => f y ^ 2) x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x ^ 2 = 0
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.jensen_gap_zero.doc: **Equality in Jensen, at every state of the chain.**

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inv.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (self : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
  (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
    ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), self.lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x =
      ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), self.lam x * f x

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.integral_eq_tsum.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 L.mu →
    ∫ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), f x ∂L.mu = ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * f x

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.instIsProbabilit.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.instIsProbabilit.doc: `μ` is a probability measure: this is `Stat.total`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.instFiniteDimens.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)),
  FiniteDimensional ℝ ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.instFiniteDimens.doc:
**`L²(λ^K)` is finite-dimensional** — the sentence of Step 4 that
`OperatorFinite.exists_resolvent` waits on.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_oneLp_self.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap), inner ℝ L.oneLp L.oneLp = 1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_oneLp_psta.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), inner ℝ L.oneLp (L.pstarLp F) = inner ℝ L.oneLp F
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_oneLp_psta.doc:
**`P⋆` preserves the mean on `L²`.** This is `λ`-invariance, tested against a
square-integrable function.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_oneLp.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), inner ℝ L.oneLp F = ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * ↑↑F x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_oneLp.doc: **`Π`, read as an inner product.** `⟪1, F⟫ = ∫ F dλ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_eq_tsum_of.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  {F G : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)} {f g : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  ↑↑F =ᵐ[L.mu] f → ↑↑G =ᵐ[L.mu] g → inner ℝ F G = ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * f x * g x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_eq_tsum_of.doc:
The same, read against any representatives: off the chain `λ` vanishes, so a.e. equality of
the integrands suffices term by term.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_eq_tsum.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (F G : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), inner ℝ F G = ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * ↑↑F x * ↑↑G x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_eq_tsum.doc:
**The Bochner half of the `LpLayer` dictionary.** `⟪F,G⟫_{L²(μ)} = ∑' x, λ(x)F(x)G(x)`.

`L2.integrable_inner` makes the pointwise product integrable, `integral_countable` turns the
integral into a sum over the countable `St`, and `Stat.mu_singleton` evaluates the weight.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_densL2_lef.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (U V : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  inner ℝ ((L.densL2 hrow) U) V = inner ℝ U ((L.pstarL2 hrow) V)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.inner_densL2_lef.doc:
**`⟪PU, V⟫ = ⟪U, P⋆V⟫` on `L²(μ)`** — `Stat.tsum_dens_mul_sq` read through the inner
product.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hitInt_succ_sub.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (n : ℕ),
  L.hitInt (n + 1) - L.hitInt n =
    1 - L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0) - (1 + GFNBounds.Doubling.sbar S cap n) * L.lam GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hitInt_succ_sub.doc: **The one-step identity.** `a_{n+1} − a_n = 1 − λ(s₀) − (1 + σ̄⁽ⁿ⁾) λ(s_f)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hitInt_mono.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap), Monotone L.hitInt

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hitInt_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)) {c : ℝ},
  c < 1 → (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / (↑j + 1)) → 0 < c → ∀ (n : ℕ), L.hitInt n ≤ ↑K / (1 - c)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hitInt_le.doc:
On the truncation the supersolution is bounded by `K/(1−c)`, which is what makes the
hitting integrals converge.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hitInt.type: {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} → {cap : Option ℕ} → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap → ℕ → ℝ

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_tailShift.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (m : ℕ),
  HasSum (fun k => L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (k + m))) (L.tailMass m)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_tailShift.doc: The tail mass is the tail of a summable series over the ladder.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_tailMass.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (m : ℕ),
  HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.tailInd cap m x) (L.tailMass m)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_one.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap), HasSum L.lam 1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_kern_flux.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St),
  HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.kern S cap x y) (L.lam y)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_flux_pt.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St),
  HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap (GFNBounds.Doubling.ptFn y) x) (L.lam y)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_flux_pt.doc: Total flux into `y` is `λ(y)`: invariance tested against the point mass at `y`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_flux.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (j : ℕ),
  HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap (GFNBounds.Doubling.dirac j) x)
    (L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j))
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_flux.doc:
**Pointwise balance, from the integral form.** `λ_j` is the total one-step flux into `j`.

This is `Stat.inv` tested against `dirac j`; the right-hand side is `λ_j` by
`tsum_lam_mul_dirac`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.hasSum_coTail.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (m : ℕ),
  HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * (1 - GFNBounds.Doubling.tailInd cap m x)) (1 - L.tailMass m)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.flux_nonneg.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (j : ℕ)
  (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), 0 ≤ L.lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap (GFNBounds.Doubling.dirac j) x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.flux_nonneg.doc: Every one-step flux term is non-negative, so a single one may be kept and the rest discarded.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.fixed_const_memL.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 L.mu →
    (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x = f x) →
      ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → f x = f (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.fixed_const_memL.doc:
**`eq:doubling_fixed`, the `P⋆` half, at the paper's hypothesis.** A fixed point of the
function action in `L²(λ)` is constant on the chain.

The ladder is climbed by the decrement alone, exactly as in `FixedPoints.fixed_const`; what is
new is that `f` is only assumed square-integrable, and the fixed-point equation only `λ`-a.e.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.fixed_const.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
    GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f = f →
      ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → f x = f (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.fixed_const.doc:
**`eq:doubling_fixed`, the `P⋆` half.** A bounded fixed point of the function action is
constant on the chain.

The ladder is climbed by the decrement alone: at a state whose doubling edge has been truncated
away the fixed-point equation gives `f(m) = f(m−1)` outright, and where it survives, equality in
Jensen gives `f(2m) = f(m−1)` and the fixed-point equation then averages the two into
`f(m) = f(m−1)`. The target row is never used.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.finset_sum_le_ta.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)) {m b : ℕ},
  b ≤ K → ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc m b, L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j) ≤ L.tailMass m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.finset_sum_le_ta.doc: A finite block of the ladder below the cap is part of the tail.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_unsolvabl.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S →
    ∃ fi fe,
      (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), 0 ≤ fi x) ∧
        (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), 0 ≤ fe x) ∧
          MeasureTheory.MemLp fi 2 L.mu ∧
            MeasureTheory.MemLp fe 2 L.mu ∧
              ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * fi x = 1 ∧
                ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.lam x * fe x = 1 ∧
                  ¬∃ f,
                      MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 L.mu ∧
                        ∀ᵐ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St) ∂L.mu, f x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S none f x = fi x - fe x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_unsolvabl.doc:
**`prop:doubling_unsolvable`(2).** There are probability densities `f_init, f_term ∈ L²(λ)`
whose difference is not a flow-matching defect: no `f ∈ L²(λ)` has `(Id − P⋆)f = f_init − f_term`.

The pair is not explicit: it is built from a `ψ ∈ ker Π` outside the range of `Id − P⋆`, and that
`ψ` exists only because the range is proper (`defectRange_ne_kerPi`), which is an open-mapping
argument.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_tailRatio.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S →
    ∀ (Q : ℝ) (m₁ : ℕ), ∃ m, m₁ ≤ m ∧ Q * L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad m) < L.tailMass m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_tailRatio.doc:
**Step 1 of `theo:doubling_unbounded`(2).** Under (★) the ratio `L(m)/λ_m` is unbounded above
*every* cut: an exponentially decaying tail would force `Σ_{i<D} log(1/ε(2^i))` to grow like `2^D`,
which (★) forbids.

The start `m₁` is a parameter, which is the paper's "dropping finitely many cuts from the supremum
leaves it infinite" — proved rather than asserted.

⚠ weakened hypothesis: no relation between `m₁` and `d` is needed. The paper's supremum runs over
`m > d`; the decay argument never uses that, because the geometric bound starts at `m₁` and the
lower bound `λ_{2^D} ≥ λ_1 ∏ ε(2^i)` starts at `1`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_small_mas.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S →
    ∀ {p : ℝ},
      1 ≤ p →
        ∀ {t : ℝ},
          0 < t →
            ∃ m,
              S.d < m ∧
                (L.mass p fun x => L.centredTail m x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S none (L.centredTail m) x) ≤
                  t * L.mass p (L.centredTail m)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_small_mas.doc:
**`eq:doubling_inf`.** For every `t > 0` some centred tail indicator has flow-matching defect
of mass at most `t` times its own mass: the infimum of the Rayleigh quotient over the mean-zero
functions of unit norm is `0`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_small_def.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S → ∀ {t : ℝ}, 0 < t → ∃ F ∈ L.kerPi, F ≠ 0 ∧ ‖L.defect F‖ ^ 2 ≤ t * ‖F‖ ^ 2
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_small_def.doc:
**`eq:doubling_inf` at `p = 2`, in `L²(λ)`.** For every `t > 0` some non-zero mean-zero class
has `‖(Id − P⋆)F‖² ≤ t‖F‖²`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_rayleigh_.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) {c₁ c₂ : ℝ},
  0 < c₁ →
    (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → c₁ * ↑j ^ (-D.p) ≤ L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j)) →
      (∀ (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j) ≤ c₂ * ↑j ^ (-D.p)) →
        ∃ m₂,
          S.d < m₂ ∧
            ∀ (m : ℕ),
              m₂ ≤ m →
                (c₁ * ↑m * L.mass 2 fun x => L.centredTail m x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S none (L.centredTail m) x) ≤
                  4 * c₂ * (D.p - 1) * L.mass 2 (L.centredTail m)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_rayleigh_.doc:
**`cor:doubling_family`.** The cut `m₂` past which the rate holds exists, because
`L(m) → 0`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_diffusion.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K))
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S (some K)),
  ∃ R,
    (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow + L.piL2) * R = 1 ∧
      R * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow + L.piL2) = 1 ∧
        (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) * (R - L.piL2) = 1 - L.piL2 ∧
          (R - L.piL2) * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) = 1 - L.piL2 ∧ L.piL2 * (R - L.piL2) = 0 ∧ (R - L.piL2) * L.piL2 = 0
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_diffusion.doc:
**`lem:doubling_operator`(2), instantiated.** On the truncation `Id − P⋆ + Π` is invertible and
the diffusion operator `S := (Id − P⋆ + Π)^{-1} − Π` satisfies `eq:doubling_resolvent`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_centredRa.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (N : ℕ), ∃ x, ↑N / 2 ≤ |L.centredRamp N x|
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_centredRa.doc:
**`eq:doubling_ramp`, first line.** The centred ramp attains `N/2` in absolute value: the two
values `r_N(s₀) = 0` and `r_N(N) = N` are both attained, so one of `Π r_N` and `N − Π r_N` is at
least `N/2`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_bhat.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K))
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S (some K)),
  ∃ Sop,
    (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) * Sop = 1 - L.piL2 ∧
      Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) = 1 - L.piL2 ∧
        L.piL2 * Sop = 0 ∧
          Sop * L.piL2 = 0 ∧ ∀ (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), ‖F - L.piL2 F‖ ≤ ‖Sop‖ * ‖F - (L.pstarL2 hrow) F‖
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.exists_bhat.doc:
**`lem:doubling_truncation_irreducible` Step 4, and `cor:doubling_truncation` Step 1.**

There is a diffusion operator `S` on `L²(λ^K)` satisfying `eq:doubling_resolvent`, and its norm
`B̂_K` is a real number — which is `B̂_K < +∞`. The last clause is what Step 3 of
`cor:doubling_truncation` consumes: `‖F − ΠF‖ = ‖S(Id − P⋆)F‖ ≤ B̂_K‖(Id − P⋆)F‖`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.evalChain_inject.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)), Function.Injective ⇑L.evalChain
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.evalChain_inject.doc:
Evaluation on the chain is injective: `λ` charges every state of the chain and vanishes off
it, so a class vanishing there is the zero class.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.evalChain.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {K : ℕ} →
    (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)) →
      ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) →ₗ[ℝ] { x // GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain (some K) x } → ℝ
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.evalChain.doc:
**Evaluation at the states of the chain**, as a linear map into a finite product. It is linear
because a.e. equality is equality on the chain (`Stat.ae_iff_eq`), so the representative of a sum
*is* the sum of the representatives there.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eq_zero_of_mem_k.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) {F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)},
  F ∈ L.kerPi → L.pstarLp F = F → F = 0

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eq_smul_oneLp_of.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) {F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)},
  (L.pstarL2 hrow) F = F → F = ↑↑F (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0) • L.oneLp
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eq_smul_oneLp_of.doc:
A fixed point of `P⋆` in `L²(λ)` is a constant class — `lem:doubling_fixed_points`' `P⋆` half
(`Stat.fixed_const_memLp`), transported to `Lp` at an arbitrary cap.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eq_smul_oneLp_of.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) {F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)},
  L.pstarLp F = F → F = ↑↑F (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0) • L.oneLp
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eq_smul_oneLp_of.doc:
A fixed point of `P⋆` in `L²(λ)` is a constant class: `lem:doubling_fixed_points`, `P⋆` half,
transported to `Lp`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_two_psta.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 L.mu →
    MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f) 2 L.mu ≤ MeasureTheory.eLpNorm f 2 L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_two_psta.doc:
**`P⋆` is a contraction of `L²(μ)`** — the `p = 2` case of `lem:doubling_operator`(1)'s
first clause.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_pstar_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ {p : ENNReal},
      1 ≤ p →
        ∀ {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
          MeasureTheory.MemLp f p L.mu →
            MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f) p L.mu ≤ MeasureTheory.eLpNorm f p L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_pstar_le.doc:
**`lem:doubling_operator`(1), first clause, in one statement.** `P⋆` is a contraction of
`L^p(μ)` for every `p ∈ [1,∞]`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_pstar_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {p : ENNReal},
  1 ≤ p →
    p ≠ ⊤ →
      ∀ {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
        MeasureTheory.MemLp f p L.mu →
          MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f) p L.mu ≤ MeasureTheory.eLpNorm f p L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_pstar_le.doc:
**`lem:doubling_operator`(1), first clause, at finite `p`.** `P⋆` is a contraction of
`L^p(μ)` for every `p ∈ [1,∞)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_dens_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ {p : ENNReal},
      1 ≤ p →
        p ≠ ⊤ →
          ∀ {u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
            MeasureTheory.MemLp u p L.mu → MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (L.dens u) p L.mu ≤ MeasureTheory.eLpNorm u p L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNorm_dens_le.doc:
**`P` is a contraction of `L^p(μ)`**, `p ∈ [1,∞)` — the `eLpNorm` form of
`Stat.mass_dens_le`. In particular `P` is a bounded operator of `L²(λ)`, which is what
`lem:doubling_operator`(1) needs of it.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNormEssSup_ps.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
      MeasureTheory.eLpNormEssSup (GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f) L.mu ≤ MeasureTheory.eLpNormEssSup f L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.eLpNormEssSup_ps.doc:
**`lem:doubling_operator`(1), first clause, at `p = ∞`.** `P⋆` is a contraction of
`L^∞(μ)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_smul.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (c : ℝ)
  (u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ), L.dens (c • u) = c • L.dens u

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_sink.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
  L.dens u GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink = u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_sink.doc: `P` at the sink: the wrap is the only incoming edge, so `(Pu)(s_f) = u(s₀)`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_lad.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ)
  (k : ℕ),
  L.dens u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad k) =
    L.w1 k * u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (k + 1)) + L.w2 k * u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad (k / 2)) +
      L.w3 k * u GFNBounds.Doubling.St.sink
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_lad.doc: `P` at a ladder state, as a three-atom average.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_gap_zero.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ {u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
      (Summable fun x => |u x| ^ 2 * L.lam x) →
        (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → L.dens u x = u x) →
          ∀ {y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St}, GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap y → L.dens (fun z => u z ^ 2) y = L.dens u y ^ 2
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_gap_zero.doc:
**The Jensen gap of `P` vanishes on the chain at a fixed point in `L²(λ)`.**

The gap is non-negative pointwise and its `λ`-integral is zero, `P` preserving the `λ`-integral
and `Pu = u` on the chain; a convergent sum of non-negative terms vanishing forces each term to.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_fixed_of_co.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → u x = u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0)) →
    ∀ {y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St}, GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap y → L.dens u y = u y
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_fixed_of_co.doc: The converse inclusion: `P` fixes every function constant on the chain.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_fixed_const.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ {u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
      (Summable fun x => |u x| ^ 2 * L.lam x) →
        (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → L.dens u x = u x) →
          ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → u x = u (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad 0)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_fixed_const.doc:
**`eq:doubling_fixed`, the `P` half.** A fixed point of the density action in `L²(λ)` is
constant on the chain.

Equality in Jensen for the reversed law makes `u` constant on the atoms of positive weight, and
the climbing atom `j ↦ j+1` has positive weight at every `j` with `j+1` on the chain: the ladder
is climbed from the source, exactly as `FixedPoints.fixed_const` descends it.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_const.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap →
    ∀ {y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St}, GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap y → L.dens (fun x => 1) y = 1
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_const.doc: **`P` fixes the constants** on the chain: the reversed law is a probability.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_congr_onCha.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  {u v : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → u x = v x) →
    ∀ (y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), L.dens u y = L.dens v y
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_congr_onCha.doc:
**`P` descends to `λ`-classes**, and unlike `P⋆` it needs no hypothesis to do so: each of its
three weights carries the factor `λ` of the state it reads (`Stat.w1`, `Stat.w2`, `Stat.w3`), so a
state off the chain is read with weight zero.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens_add.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (u v : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ), L.dens (u + v) = L.dens u + L.dens v

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densLp_smul.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (c : ℝ) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  L.densLp hrow (c • F) = c • L.densLp hrow F

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densLp_add.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (F G : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  L.densLp hrow (F + G) = L.densLp hrow F + L.densLp hrow G

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densLp.congr_sim.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (F F_1 : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  F = F_1 → L.densLp hrow F = L.densLp hrow F_1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densLp.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} →
    (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) →
      GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densLp.doc: `P` acting on `L²(μ)`, as a map of the space into itself.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densL2_mul_piL2.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap), L.densL2 hrow * L.piL2 = L.piL2
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densL2_mul_piL2.doc: `P Π = Π`, read off the adjoint of `Π P⋆ = Π`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densL2_apply.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), (L.densL2 hrow) F = L.densLp hrow F

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densL2.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} →
    (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) →
      GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.densL2.doc:
**`P` as a bounded linear operator on `L²(μ)`**, of norm at most `1` — the mirror of
`Stat.pstarL2`, and the operator the paper's `β̂ₙ` is measured on.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap → (GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ) → GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.dens.doc:
**The density action** `Pu := d((uλ)T)/dλ`, in closed form: the transported measure `(uλ)T`
of `Balance.mact`, divided by `λ`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defect_sub_mean.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  L.defect (F - inner ℝ L.oneLp F • L.oneLp) = L.defect F

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defect_oneLp.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none), L.defect L.oneLp = 0

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defect_apply.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  L.defect F = F - L.pstarLp F

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defectRange_ne_k.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.GrowthCond S → L.defectRange ≠ L.kerPi
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defectRange_ne_k.doc:
**`prop:doubling_unsolvable`(1), the proper half.** `(Id − P⋆)L²(λ)` is not all of `ker Π`:
were it, the open mapping theorem would bound `Id − P⋆` below on `ker Π`, against
`eq:doubling_inf`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defectRange_le_k.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none), L.defectRange ≤ L.kerPi
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defectRange_le_k.doc: The defect of any class has zero mean: `Π(Id − P⋆) = 0`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defectRange.type: {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} → (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) → Submodule ℝ ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defect.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) → ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) →L[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.defect.doc: **`Id − P⋆`** as a bounded operator of `L²(λ)`, on the loop closure.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.decayK.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)),
  (∀ (j : ℕ), S.eps j = D.eps j) →
    ∀ {ℓ : ℕ},
      S.d < ℓ →
        1 ≤ ℓ →
          4 * ℓ ≤ K →
            ∀ {Z₁ Z₂ : ℝ},
              0 < Z₁ →
                0 < Z₂ →
                  (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → Z₁ ≤ D.descOne ℓ y) →
                    (∀ (y : ℕ), ℓ ≤ y → D.descOne ℓ y ≤ Z₂) →
                      ∃ Cm Cp,
                        0 < Cm ∧
                          Cp ≤ Z₂ / Z₁ * 2 ^ D.p * ((1 - S.epsMax)⁻¹ ^ ℓ + ((D.c / (2 * ↑ℓ + 1)) ^ ℓ)⁻¹) ^ 2 * Cm ∧
                            ∀ (m : ℕ),
                              ℓ ≤ m →
                                m ≤ K / 2 →
                                  Cm * ↑m ^ (-D.p) ≤ L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad m) ∧
                                    L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad m) ≤ Cp * ↑m ^ (-D.p)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.decayK.doc:
**`eq:doubling_decayK`.** Two constants sandwiching `λ^K` on `[ℓ, K/2]`, with a ratio
`C⁺/C⁻ ≤ (Z₂/Z₁) 2^{p_*} Q²` **free of `K`** — which is the `c₉` of the paper, since `Q` depends
on `c` and `ℓ` alone and `Z₁, Z₂` on `c` and `d` alone.

Stated with `Z₁ ≤ E(Z_ℓ) ≤ Z₂` — `eq:doubling_product` at the level `ℓ` — as hypotheses, which
`Decay.descOne_two_sided` (`Product.lean`) discharges for every `ℓ ≥ m₀`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.cutBalanceSeq_tr.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)),
  GFNBounds.Doubling.CutBalanceSeq S (fun j => L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j)) ↑(K / 2)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.cutBalanceSeq_tr.doc: The truncation's masses satisfy `eq:doubling_cut` up to `K/2`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.ctorIdx.type: {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} → {cap : Option ℕ} → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap → ℕ

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.coeFn_sub_pstarL.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) {f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ} (hf : MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 L.mu),
  ↑↑(MeasureTheory.MemLp.toLp f hf - (L.pstarL2 hrow) (MeasureTheory.MemLp.toLp f hf)) =ᵐ[L.mu] fun x =>
    f x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.coeFn_sub_pstarL.doc: The defect class of the class of `f` is the class of the pointwise defect.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.coeFn_pstarLp.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)), ↑↑(L.pstarLp F) =ᵐ[L.mu] GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap ↑↑F

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.coeFn_pstarL2.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  ↑↑((L.pstarL2 hrow) F) =ᵐ[L.mu] GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap ↑↑F

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.coeFn_oneLp.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap), ↑↑L.oneLp =ᵐ[L.mu] fun x => 1

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.coeFn_densLp.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  ↑↑(L.densLp hrow F) =ᵐ[L.mu] L.dens ↑↑F

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.coeFn_densL2.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  ↑↑((L.densL2 hrow) F) =ᵐ[L.mu] L.dens ↑↑F

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.coeFn_defect.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (F : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 L.mu)),
  ↑↑(L.defect F) =ᵐ[L.mu] fun x => ↑↑F x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S none (↑↑F) x

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.coTail_pos.type: ∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) {m : ℕ}, 1 < m → 0 < 1 - L.tailMass m
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.coTail_pos.doc: `1 − L(m) ≥ λ_1 > 0` for `m > 1`: the state `1` is outside the tail.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.centredTail_boun.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (m : ℕ),
  ∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |L.centredTail m x| ≤ C
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.centredTail_boun.doc: The centred tail indicator is bounded, hence a legitimate test function.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.centredTail.type: {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} → {cap : Option ℕ} → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap → ℕ → GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.centredRamp_defe.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (N : ℕ) (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St),
  L.centredRamp N x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S none (L.centredRamp N) x =
    GFNBounds.Doubling.rampFn N x - GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S none (GFNBounds.Doubling.rampFn N) x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.centredRamp_defe.doc: Centring leaves the defect unchanged: `P⋆` fixes the constants.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.centredRamp_boun.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none) (N : ℕ),
  ∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |L.centredRamp N x| ≤ C

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.centredRamp.type: {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S none → ℕ → GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.centredRamp.doc: `r̃_N := r_N − Π r_N`, the centred clipped ramp.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.casesOn.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} →
    {motive : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap → Sort u} →
      (t : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) →
        ((lam : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ) →
            (nonneg : ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), 0 ≤ lam x) →
              (pos : ∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → 0 < lam x) →
                (vanish : ∀ ⦃x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St⦄, ¬GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → lam x = 0) →
                  (summable : Summable lam) →
                    (total : ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x = 1) →
                      (inv :
                          ∀ (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
                            (∃ C, ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), |f x| ≤ C) →
                              ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x * GFNBounds.Doubling.pstar S cap f x =
                                ∑' (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), lam x * f x) →
                        motive
                          { lam := lam, nonneg := nonneg, pos := pos, vanish := vanish, summable := summable,
                            total := total, inv := inv }) →
          motive t

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.block_ratio.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {K : ℕ} (D : GFNBounds.Doubling.Decay) (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S (some K)),
  (∀ (j : ℕ), S.eps j = D.eps j) →
    ∀ {ℓ : ℕ},
      S.d < ℓ →
        1 ≤ ℓ →
          4 * ℓ ≤ K →
            ∀ {j j' : ℕ},
              ℓ ≤ j →
                j < 2 * ℓ →
                  ℓ ≤ j' →
                    j' < 2 * ℓ →
                      L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j') ≤
                        ((1 - S.epsMax)⁻¹ ^ ℓ + ((D.c / (2 * ↑ℓ + 1)) ^ ℓ)⁻¹) * L.lam (GFNBounds.Doubling.St.lad j)
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.block_ratio.doc:
**The block ratio, free of `K`.** On `[ℓ, 2ℓ)` any two masses differ by at most
`Q = ρ^ℓ + (η^ℓ)^{-1}`, with `ρ = (1−ε_max)^{-1}` and `η = c/(2ℓ+1)` — constants of `c` and `ℓ`
alone. This is what makes `c₉` independent of the cap.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.betaHat.type:
{S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} →
  {cap : Option ℕ} → GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap → GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap → ℕ → ℝ
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.betaHat.doc:
**`β̂ₙ := ‖Pⁿ − Π‖_{L²(λ)}`** — the mixing coefficient of `def:doubling_setting`, defined on
the density action as the paper defines it.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.aestronglyMeasur.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) (f : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ),
  MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable f L.mu
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.aestronglyMeasur.doc: Every function on `St` is measurable, the σ-algebra being discrete.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.ae_iff_onChain.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  {p : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → Prop},
  (∀ᵐ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St) ∂L.mu, p x) ↔ ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → p x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.ae_iff_onChain.doc: **The bridge, for a predicate.** A `μ`-a.e. property is a property of the chain.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.ae_iff_eq.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  {f g : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  f =ᵐ[L.mu] g ↔ ∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → f x = g x
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.ae_iff_eq.doc:
**The bridge.** `f =ᵐ[μ] g` iff `f` and `g` agree at every state of the chain.

`λ` charges every on-chain state (`Stat.pos`) and vanishes off it (`Stat.vanish`), so the only
`μ`-null set meeting the chain is empty. On the loop closure `OnChain` is vacuous and a.e.
equality is equality.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.ae_eq_of_onChain.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  {f g : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : GFNBounds.Doubling.St), GFNBounds.Doubling.OnChain cap x → f x = g x) → f =ᵐ[L.mu] g
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.ae_eq_of_onChain.doc: Equality on the chain gives a.e. equality — the direction the `Lp` constructions consume.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.adjoint_pstarL2.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap), ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (L.pstarL2 hrow) = L.densL2 hrow
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.adjoint_pstarL2.doc:
**The adjoint clause of `lem:doubling_operator`(1).** The density action is the `L²(λ)`-adjoint
of the function action.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.adjoint_piL2.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap),
  ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint L.piL2 = L.piL2

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.adjoint_densL2_p.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap) (n : ℕ),
  ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (L.densL2 hrow ^ n - L.piL2) = L.pstarL2 hrow ^ n - L.piL2
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.adjoint_densL2_p.doc: `P⋆ⁿ − Π` is the adjoint of `Pⁿ − Π`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.adjoint_densL2.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap)
  (hrow : GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain S cap), ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (L.densL2 hrow) = L.pstarL2 hrow
GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.adjoint_densL2.doc: The same identity read the other way: `P* = P⋆`.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.abs_rpow_dens_le.type:
∀ {S : GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat S cap) {p : ℝ},
  1 ≤ p →
    ∀ (u : GFNBounds.Doubling.St → ℝ) {y : GFNBounds.Doubling.St},

GFNBounds.Doubling.Stat.doc:
An invariant probability of the chain in play — `λ` of `def:doubling_setting`.

Positivity is **on chain**, and `λ` vanishes off it; see `OnChain`. On the loop closure
`OnChain` is vacuous and this is the paper's "positive at every state".

Invariance is carried in the **integral** form `∫ P⋆f dλ = ∫ f dλ` against bounded `f`, which is
the form every downstream use consumes (`prop:doubling_cut` tests it against `1_A`) and which
needs no summability side condition at the point of use. The pointwise form `λT = λ` is
equivalent on a countable space; that bridge is `inv_of_pointwise` in `PointwiseInv.lean`.

Positivity is a field rather than a theorem because every statement of the appendix downstream of
`lem:doubling_irreducible` quantifies over "an invariant probability" — the existence question is
`prop:doubling_phase`, which is separate and, for the family, hard.

GFNBounds.Doubling.Setting.doc:
The standing hypotheses of `def:doubling_setting`, minus the family.

The target row `P̂_B(s_f → ·)` is finitely supported **by hypothesis** (`row_supp`), so every
expression involving it is a `Finset.sum` and never a `tsum`; that kills a class of summability
side conditions before it appears.

`epsMax` is a field rather than `⨆ j, eps j` because the appendix only ever uses
`ε(j) ≤ ε_max < 1`, and an `iSup` in `ℝ` would drag `BddAbove` bookkeeping through every proof.
`lem:doubling_range` supplies `ε_max = c·2^(-s)` for the family.

GFNBounds.Doubling.RowOnChain.doc:
The target row reaches only states of the chain.

Vacuous on the loop closure; on the truncation at `K` it is `d ≤ K`, which
`cor:doubling_truncation` assumes anyway (it takes `K ≥ 2d`). It is what makes `P⋆` descend to
`λ`-classes: the sink reads `f` at `1, …, d`, and off the chain a.e. equality says nothing.
